entries.label: 石斧
entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE single transparent inventory/held-tool sprite for FlatWorld, part of the same approved handmade axe set.
Reference roles: Image 1 is the newly approved BRONZE AXE and is the authoritative set-consistency reference: MATCH its overall size/framing, diagonal pose, silhouette readability, block size, wooden haft, and coarse rope-lashing language. Image 2 is the approved current bear reinforcing LARGE PIXEL BLOCKS and broad connected color masses. Image 3 is the native player body reinforcing coarse in-game pixel density. Image 4 is this axe's current source sprite for material identity only; REDRAW it at Image 1's style.
CRITICAL: genuinely COARSE chunky pixel art, not high-definition pixel art. The whole axe uses only about 26-30 LARGE square logical cells along its longest dimension on a roughly 32x32 conceptual grid, presented as greatly enlarged clean square blocks. Outline, shaft, rope, blade and every highlight all share the SAME coarse logical grid. Low saturation, few connected broad color fields, one main shadow region and one broad restrained highlight. Do not add tiny details within the blocks: NO fine wood grain, scratches, cracks, rope fibres, tiny patina spots, small sparkling highlights, fine gradients, antialiasing, blur, texture overlay, or high-resolution painting with a pixel filter.
Composition: exactly one complete axe, handle heel bottom-left and head upper-right at about 45 degrees, blade faces RIGHT, matched to Image 1. Centered, transparent margin, all parts visible, upper-left light. Warm brown slightly uneven wooden handle, head secured in a notched/split haft using two or three BROAD tan rope turns with a chunky simple knot at the ACTUAL head/wood joint. Primitive hand assembly, no machined metal socket, modern screws or industrial fitting. Do not add decoration, sheath, pedestals, labels, borders, floor, cast shadow, extra items, a grid or animation variants. True transparent alpha.
Subject: STONE AXE (石斧). The recipe is ordinary stone + wood sticks + rope. A heavy, rough gray-brown ordinary stone axe head, somewhat rounded/irregular stone wedge with a broad working edge facing right, visibly stone rather than metal. Only two or three LARGE broad earthy gray stone faces and a restrained pale-gray edge face; keep ordinary stone warmer/grayer and blunter than a dark sharp flint blade. Rope across the stone/haft joint is functional. Use a natural asymmetrical primitive stone silhouette, not the bronze head merely recolored. No stone-grain dots, many small chips, thin cracks or shiny metallic bevel.

A sturdy thick slightly uneven early crude iron chopper head, dark charcoal gray / muted graphite with two large flat faces and one dull gray cutting bevel. Rough workmanship is expressed ONLY by a slightly asymmetrical chunky outline and broad uneven dark/light fields, not by tiny pits or many scratches.
